intro: Every card kind and zone from the stage-1 inventory, **today beside the prototype**, at 1600 and at 390. The proposed crops are screenshots of `proto/session-view.html` (stage 5) taken by the same instrument, with the same crop rule and the same names as today's, so the two columns cannot disagree about what was built.
howToRead: Each pair says the kind, the state, the principles (P1–P10) and breaks (B1–B13, grammar.md §1 and §7) that changed it, and one sentence on what changed. **Where the proposal reads worse than today, an amber note says so** — those are the most useful lines on the page. A kind the prototype did not convert, or that only a live document shows, says so instead of showing a fake. Click any image for the full-size crop. Timestamps differ between the columns because the fixture stamps *now*. At 390 both columns show the dev switch and, on the charter, the phone's task sheet over the card's foot: both are fixed to the window and the crop takes what the window shows.

6.1.title: 🪶 Title, settled, read by the Founder
6.1.by: P1 P3 P5 P7 · B1 B2 B5 B11 B13
6.1.text: The head is the title itself, with the paragraph's power line under it, where today it is a sentence *about* the title; who chose it becomes one grey line of text instead of a pressed blue pill; the empty *Why are you changing this?* box and the 🗑️ with nothing to put back are gone until something is typed.
6.1.worse: grammar §6.1 draws the head at the title's own size (`--h-title`); the prototype draws it at body size, so the head is the title's words but not the title as the page shows it. And the *The document is titled [A new title].* block restates the sentence form the head just dropped, so the card now names the title two ways. At 390 the head (title plus power line) and the fact line run to seven lines before the first choice.

6.2.title: A quick judgment (💡), a member, live
6.2.text: *The clause as it stands* no longer stands above the clause, so the clause opens exactly where the paragraph was and the tab stays level with it (today both drop 33 px); the words move into the lane as *Current text* and *Proposed*, beside the radios.
6.2.worse: the reader now learns that the second block is the proposal only after reading all of it and its rationale — *Proposed* sits by the radio at the block's foot, small and grey, where today it heads the block.

6.3.title: A sealed record (✔), a text change not yet read — fixture stand-in
6.3.text: §6.3 names a live record; the fixture's `race-claims` stands in. The *DECIDED · 7/14* dateline moves from above the clause to one fact line under the winner's rationale, so the clause lands level with its ✔ tab (today 62–84 px lower); the rivals lose their boxes and are divided by hairlines.
6.3.worse: *Previous text* and each rival's share still stand as small labels **above** their blocks, at the right — the one label position O1 (a) was meant to retire — and without today's dashed box the previous text is told from the rivals by that label alone. At 390 the one fact line wraps to four lines.

6.4.title: A constitutional motion (👤), a member who is not the mover
6.4.by: P3 P5 P7 · B1 B5 · O1 (a)
6.4.text: The standing rule keeps its *Prefer this* lane (Q1362's peer) and gains a *Current rule* label and a provenance line; the 🗑️ with nothing to put back is gone, so the row is the 🏛️ commit alone.
6.4.worse: the card is 23 px taller than today for one extra line of provenance, and that line sits between the current rule's radio and the proposal, where it reads as a caption for the proposal below it as easily as for the rule above.

6.5.title: ✉️ Invite, a member, at the all-members price
6.5.text: The empty rationale box under the empty address box and the 🗑️ with nothing to discard are gone; the price sentence and the address box are all the card holds until an address is typed.
6.5.worse: the head's empty wording changed from the sentence *Nobody has been invited yet.* to the bracketed *(no outstanding invitations)* — CP6's people-head form, but it reads as a placeholder rather than as the document speaking.
